Film concepts for Kier and Beau.

Updated Wed 18 Nov, 9:33pm

Just concepts

Nothing is made yet.

These are the architect renders, used to show the idea. In the real films every scene is rebuilt as a clean, high-quality vertical shot with real-looking light and people, so it will look far better than these.

  • 2 finished films (10 to 20 seconds) and 5 short clips (6 to 10 seconds)
  • Tall 9:16, made for phones
  • Finished with custom music and sound effects, ready to post
  • Every image and clip in one folder
  • Each one ends on “AI concept film”

1Film 1 · 18 seconds · Woman 1

Day one in Seseh

She opens the curtains to the sea, picks up her keys at reception, and ends her first day with a sunset drink on the roof.

Why it sells: Buyers picture their own first day here. That feeling is what turns a scroll into an enquiry.

2Film 2 · 20 seconds · Woman 2

Life at Seseh pace

A drone rises over the rice fields to the sea. Then one unhurried day: coffee on the penthouse balcony, a massage, sunset in the rooftop bar.

Why it sells: It sells calm and being looked after, which is what second-home buyers are really paying for.

3Clip 1 · 8 seconds · Woman 1

Heat, then ice

Steam bursts off the sauna rocks. She walks through it, drops into the ice bath and comes up laughing.

Why it sells: Wellness built into the building, shown in one rush. The kind of clip people replay and send to a friend.

4Clip 2 · 7 seconds · Woman 2

Tee off downstairs

A clean swing in Segara's golf simulator, the ball lands on the green, and she turns with a grin.

Why it sells: A private extra most Bali homes don't have, with no traffic to get to it.

5Clip 3 · 8 seconds · No people

Dawn to lanterns

One still camera on the rooftop pool as the whole day passes: blue dawn, morning sun, gold sunset, lanterns at night.

Why it sells: It shows the rooftop at its best in every light, and the calm pace keeps people watching to the end.

Logged off, straight in

She closes her laptop in the co-working lounge, crosses the rooftop and slips into the infinity pool as the sun sets.

Why it sells: Remote workers are a big Seseh buyer group. Work and the good life, under one roof.

Wake up to the sea

From the pillow: white sheets, curtains drifting, then the sea and palms through the open doors.

Why it sells: The view is why people buy in Seseh. It loops back to the start, so it plays again and gets saved.
